claims.text: High configurational entropy in AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 induces significant lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion promotes rapid, selective outward diffusion of Al and Cr.
Outward diffusion of oxidation-active elements causes nucleation and growth of a coherent protective oxide scale.
AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 forms an oxide scale composed primarily of CrTaO4.
The oxide scale contains dispersed Al2O3 and Cr2O3 phases.
The resulting oxide scale is dense and adherent.
A continuous CrTaO4 layer impedes inward oxygen diffusion and outward diffusion of substrate elements.
The synergy between configurational entropy, lattice distortion, and selective oxidation governs oxidation resistance more strongly than the absolute amount of oxidation-active elements.
Reducing Al and Cr concentrations provides a baseline that isolates configurational-entropy effects from elemental-composition effects.
The full-composition alloy is expected to have greater lattice distortion than the modified alloy.
Greater measured lattice distortion correlated with better oxide-scale performance would confirm a causal role for configurational entropy.
The full-composition alloy will exhibit lower weight gain than the modified alloy.
The full-composition alloy will exhibit parabolic oxidation kinetics.
The full-composition alloy will form a more uniform and adherent scale than the modified alloy.
The full-composition alloy will show self-healing after mechanical or thermal stress.
The proposed mechanism applies to AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 during atmospheric oxidation at 1000–1100 °C for up to 200 hours.
Enhanced diffusion kinetics at 1100 °C can promote homogeneous growth of a continuous CrTaO4 layer.

contradictions.description: The stated alloy AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 contains no Ta, yet its proposed principal oxide is CrTaO4. No Ta source or Ta-containing modification is specified.

The baseline changes Al and Cr concentrations while being claimed to isolate configurational entropy from composition. This directly confounds entropy/lattice-distortion effects with oxidation-active-element content, and no composition-matched control is specified.

The mechanism and falsification rule require oxide performance to correlate with lattice distortion, whereas the predicted-outcome field says that differences remaining after lattice distortion is quantified support configurational entropy. Merely persisting after measurement does not establish the required correlation.
